# Navvi

> Compile it once so you never drive it again. Navvi is a self-healing scraper compiler: `npx navvi "<prompt>" <url...>` turns a plain-words request and a few URLs into JSON records and a compiled scraper file. The first run asks a small number of multiple-choice questions about the page (answered by the host coding agent with no API key, or by Jev / any AI SDK model with one); every later run replays the compiled scraper with zero model calls and heals a moved field or a renamed button instead of failing. Secrets stay in the environment, logins use a local browser profile, and the tool never solves captchas or runs model output as code.

## Start here

- [SKILL.md](SKILL.md): the agent skill. The one command, the no-key question protocol on stdio, the file-and-resume path (exit 3), input contract, output shape, exit codes and limits.
- [README: Install and run](README.md#install-and-run): four lines from zero to data.
- [README: What you get](README.md#what-you-get): records, the scraper JSON you can commit, the zero-model second run.
- [README: Choosers](README.md#choosers): claude and codex (an installed, signed-in CLI on your subscription), jev, model, agent (no key), and what each needs.
- [README: Exit codes](README.md#exit-codes): what each status means and what to do next.
- [README: Limits](README.md#limits): drift versus redesign, captchas, logins and secrets.

## Reference

- `npx navvi --help`: every flag in one screen.
- `storage/key_value_stores/scraper-cache/<cacheKey>.json`: the compiled scraper produced by a run.
- `storage/questions/<token>.json`: a parked question batch waiting for `--answers <file> --resume <token>`.
- [docs/measurements.md](docs/measurements.md): questions, wait time and cost with and without Jev on the same pages.
- [LICENSE](LICENSE): MIT.
